all_comments.text: Even from Nike's own presentation you can tell this AF4 is being marketed as the shoe suitable for all runners from elites to those running 5+ hours. AF3 was undeniably the general people's choice for marathons and half marathons. Every race you go to close to a third if not half the people had them on. The AF4 will step right into that space and eat up all those sales again, while their new shoe with actual new tech (I'm thinking full length zoom x LT with some other geometry changes and pod changes) will satisfy the majority of the non-elite but competitive runner market.

all_comments.text:
Thank you for dropping this early review! I appreciate someone who actually spends their own money, races in a shoe, and keeps it real instead of calling EVERYTHING they test a "banger" or speaks glowingly about a product so the brand keeps sending samples. 

That being said, I'm so over Nike putting profit and legacy over advancing tech and giving it to their customers. The Nike Air units are pushing 50 years old, and the zoom air units are pushing 25. I don't care how light the shoe, give us better midsole tech and stop nickel and diming us for minimal updates that are mostly stylistic. The Pegasus line is a joke. The Alpha, Vapor, and Zoom Fly are all resting on their laurels. 

I want to be excited about the Apex, but it feels like Nike is just hyping us all up to deliver a shoe that will cost $350 but will feature midsole foams that are already available from Chinese brands right now for less than $150. Thanks for calling out the "air" tech as being dated, and hopefully bigger fellas realize there are mich better options for race day. Check out the Feidian Challeneger 5, Anta G9 2, or Qiadian Plaid 3.0 if you're a bigger guy needing a light racer.
